cards.text: Jerusalem has a problem, friend: the city is big and wide open, but there are few people in it, and the houses aren't rebuilt yet (Nehemiah 7:4). A whole city with NOBODY home? That's a cookie box with no cookies in it.

cards.question: Jerusalem needs people living inside those walls. Which group settles there?
The rest of the people take a vote to decide who else moves into Jerusalem.
Instead, the people cast lots. The lots pick ___ out of every ten people to live in Jerusalem.
After the lots are cast, the other nine out of every ten stay in their own towns.
Some men volunteer to live in Jerusalem. How do the people treat the men who volunteer?

cards.text: Then comes the roll call of who settles in Jerusalem: families from Judah and Benjamin, priests, Levites, and gatekeepers who keep watch at the gates. Every group gets a head count. Somebody was counting heads like it was their whole job, friend. Because it WAS.

Everyone else spreads out over the villages of Judah and Benjamin. Judah's people settle all the way from Beersheba to the Valley of Hinnom, and Benjamin's settle in towns like Michmash and Bethel. I spent YEARS in one drawer, and these folks get a whole map!

Next, the record goes back to the priests and Levites who went up with Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, who led the first group home from exile (Ezra 2:1-2), and with Jeshua the high priest (Haggai 1:1). It traces the priestly families down through the generations, starting with Jeshua, the father of Joiakim. It ends with Levite leaders giving praise and thanksgiving as David the man of God prescribed, and gatekeepers guarding the storerooms at the gates.
They served in the days of Joiakim son of Jeshua, and in the days of Nehemiah the governor and Ezra the priest and scribe. That's the roster, friend, but this city's story? NOT done.
